**Finding submitted: compliant (at fallback).**

Rule T4C is satisfied without a redline. The termination architecture in ¶4(a) clears the fallback on all material terms:

| Material term | Document | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Customer convenience right | Yes, 90 days' notice post-Initial Term | Fallback: 60–90 days ✓ |
| Committed lock-in | 12 months exactly (1-yr auto-renew) | Walk-away needs >12 months ✓ |
| Early-termination fee | None; only fees earned in the 90-day notice window | Fallback cap: 3 months' fees ✓ |
| Vendor convenience right | 90 days' notice | Walk-away is <90 days ✓ |

The two gaps versus the *preferred* position — 90 days rather than 30, and the Vendor's exit not being confined to the end of a renewal term — are recorded in the rationale as sub-elements, not deviations, per the classification semantics. They carry little practical weight here because the notice period is reciprocal and the renewal cycle is only twelve months, so our maximum unavoidable exposure is short.

One point worth flagging for the deal team even though it is outside this rule's scope: the absence of a prepaid-fee refund is harmless *only because* §5 (p0023) is structured as a revenue share, where Kubient collects from Advertisers and remits to us within seven days under sequential liability. If that commercial model changes to any prepaid or subscription-fee footing during negotiation, the refund gap would become live and T4C should be re-run against the revised fee clause.
